message:
fix(test): the scenario suite was deleting outside the repository and killing by name

Two things it had no authority to do, and I ran it repeatedly without
checking what it did to the machine.

It built its tree under %TEMP% and, on startup, enumerated `gnlink-scn-*`
there and remove_tree'd every match. That is deleting outside the
repository root, which the top-level rule forbids; permission to run a
test is not permission to remove files elsewhere. That the pattern
happened to match only this suite's own output is not the point -- nothing
here gets to make that judgement about a directory it does not own. The
root now comes from the build (CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR/.claude/scenario-runs) so
it cannot drift, only this run's own directory is removed, and that is
guarded by a check that the path really is under the configured root.
What earlier runs left is listed and left alone.

And the sweep terminated on the strength of a file name. Where it could
not read a process's path it assumed the process was its own -- so the
case it could not identify was the case it killed. "Nothing else on this
machine is called ScnHost.exe" is a guess about the whole machine, not
evidence about one process, and a PID can be reused between the snapshot
and the terminate. Worse, startup called it with an empty scope, which is
not a narrow scope but the absence of one: a second run of this suite
would have been shot by the first.

The path is read now, and it must be under the scope, or nothing happens.
Unidentifiable is reported, never stopped -- the same rule the product
follows for a liveness check it cannot complete. Three controls state it
rather than leaving it to be assumed: a same-named process in another
directory survives a sweep, a concurrent run's process survives a sweep,
and %TEMP% is not inside the root that may be removed.
